MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ADJOURNED MEETING
  JULY 18, 2022

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates was called to order at 6:05 p.m. at Highridge Park, 29035 Highridge Road, Rolling
  Hills Estates, California, by CHAIR CIAROLLA.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR CIAROLLA led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Bain, Ciarolla, Persichina, Pope, Romanelli,
  McCormick, and Retz

  Commissioners Absent:  None

  City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF JUNE 9,
  2022

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by
  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI to:

  APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  JUNE 9, 2022.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  B.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF JUNE 20,
  2022

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by
  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI to:

  APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  JUNE 20, 2022.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
JULY 18, 2022
   There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  NONE.

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT

  Assistant City Manager Davis gave a brief overview of the written report.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  RETZ to:

  RECOMMEND TO THE CITY COUNCIL TO ENTER INTO A
  PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT TO THE SATISFACTION OF
  THE CITY ATTORNEY WITH PAGEANTRY PRODUCTIONS TO PROVIDE
  PARADE MANAGEMENT SERVICES FOR THE PENINSULA HOLIDAY
  PARADE OF LIGHTS ON DECEMBER 3, 2022.

  AYES: Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick, Persichina, Pope, Retz, Romanelli
  NOES: None

  The motion carried.

  B.  LANDSCAPE WATER USE SURVEY

  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith provide a brief overview of the written staff
  report.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ asked what the difference in cost was between Ernie
  Howlett and Dapplegray noting the Dapplegray is a lot smaller in size than Ernie
  Howlett and the expectation would be a significant cost different. Maintenance
  Superintendent Goldsmith responded that the quote is based on sprinkler heads.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked how this project is coordinated at Highridge to
  consider the turf removal project. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith
  responded that the final project would be adjusted to accommodate changes to the
  irrigation system as a result of the approved turf replacement project. She
  additionally asked if this could be considered as part of that project for funding

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
JULY 18, 2022
   purposes to which Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith responded that
  CalWater is not funding this type of project under their current programs.

  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith briefly described the conceptual scope
  proposed for City Hall grounds in response to COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI.
  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI expressed concern with the amount of hours and
  the general not-to-exceed amount determined and explained that he would like to
  see the hours better defined to tighten a not-to-exceed figure further. Assistant City
  Manager responded that staff planned to proceed with this item to the City Council
  at its meeting the following week which is a project aligned with Council goals.
  COMMISSIONER RETZ agreed with COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI and added
  that he would be comfortable provisionally passing the recommendation as long as
  the concern was addressed as part of the City Council’s approval.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that there needs to be a way to keep the
  contractor accountable to hours and fees and a process to monitor.

  In response to COMMISSIONER BAIN, Maintenance Superintendent Gold
  explained that the goal of this irrigation audit was to assess water use in the existing
  infrastructure and determine any future upgrades that may be needed to help
  conserve water for the future.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if decorative grass areas could be
  considered. Assistant City Manager affirmed that this would be considered when
  reviewing landscape plans.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  RETZ to:

  RECOMMEND THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE A CONTRACT WITH
  WATERWISE CONSULTING FOR IRRIGATION AUDIT SERVICES AT
  ERNIE HOWLETT, HIGHRIDGE AND DAPPLEGRAY PARKS WITH THE
  ADDITIONAL CONDITION OF TIGHTER CONTROLS ON PRICING AND
  HOURS BEING REFINED TO BETTER REFLECT A NOT-TO-EXCEED
  AMOUNT.

  AYES Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick, Persichina, Pope, Retz, Romanelli
  ABSENT: None

  The motion carried.

  7.  STAFF ITEMS

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
JULY 18, 2022
   Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas reported on the status of the Hills Are
  Alive Race event coming up on Saturday, August 6, 2022.

  8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A. ADOPT-A-PARK

  NONE.

  B. MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked how the July Concert in the Park went.
  Supervisor Pinuelas responded that although attendance was light the event
  went well with approximately 100 community members in attendance and added
  that community representatives from the Palos Verdes Peninsula 4H Club,
  Palos Verdes Peninsula Senior Village, and the Palos Verdes Peninsula Land
  Conservancy were on hand to provide information to attendees.

  9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A. CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF JUNE 28, 2022.

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  10.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  NONE.

  11.  PARK TOURS

  A. HIGHRIDGE PARK

  Superintendent Goldsmith asked if the barbecue grills could be removed as they
  are not frequently used. The Commissioners agreed to removal.

  It was noted that Palos Verdes Peninsula Girls Softball has been in touch with
  staff on future improvements to the area, including a request for bleachers.

  New perimeter fencing was noticed; the approved turf removal project area was
  identified.

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR CIAROLLA MOVED TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
JULY 18, 2022
   ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 7:02 PM TO THE NEXT ADJOURNED
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING ON AUGUST 15, 2022,
  AT 6:00 P.M., WHICH BE HELD AT CHANDLER PRESERVE, 95
  BUCKSKIN LANE, ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CA 90274.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  ___________________________

  Community Services Supervisor  Chair, Park & Activities Commission
